references.title: NIST Engineering Statistics Handbook — Lognormal distribution
references.summary: NIST defines a lognormal variable as one whose logarithm is normally distributed. In the two-parameter form the density contains the squared logarithmic deviation in the negative exponent. Its log-space standard deviation corresponds to ln(sigma_g) in aerosol notation, rather than sigma_g itself. This supports checking the missing squared term in the early SAME report; it is general mathematical background, not a NASA measurement.

references.title: NIST — Moment Method for Obtaining Particle Size Measures of Test Smokes
references.scope: Publication abstract for NISTIR 7050; full report not consulted in this web pass
references.summary: The abstract describes continuous number concentration, ionization-chamber response and mass measurements for five test smokes. Moment ratios yield arithmetic mean diameter and diameter of average mass. Inferring geometric standard deviation requires a lognormal assumption. Comparisons with cascade-impactor measurements are described. The web page creation/publication label must not be substituted for the original report date without checking the report itself.

references.title: NIST — Light Scattering Characteristics and Size Distribution of Smoke and Nuisance Aerosols
references.scope: 2003 publication abstract; full paper not consulted in this web pass
references.summary: The abstract reports differential mass scattering measurements in m² g⁻¹ sr⁻¹, for two linear polarizations, angles 5–135 degrees and wavelength 632.8 nm. It describes discrimination using a 45/135-degree scattering ratio, polarization ratio and q=(4π/lambda)sin(theta/2). These are results from that study, not supplied PSI detector geometry, a universal classification rule or validation of AERO-PSI predictions.
